digest.headline: The Nasdaq suffered a record point loss as technology shares tumbled and global markets reacted to artificial intelligence concerns.

lede.b: The Nasdaq composite index dropped by 5.52% in a single session, which is a record point loss for the stock market measure of technology companies. This happened because investors worried about artificial intelligence and United States midterm politics, causing them to sell shares. Government bond yields, which are the returns paid on loans made to the government, drifted lower as traders sought safer assets. Meanwhile, gold headed for its biggest weekly gain since August.
lede.i: The Nasdaq composite index fell by 5.52% in a record single-session point loss driven by artificial intelligence concerns and United States midterm anxieties. Major technology shares plummeted across the board, triggering a broad equity sell-off. Government bond yields drifted lower as market participants sought safety in fixed income, while gold headed for its largest weekly gain since August.
lede.a: The Nasdaq composite tumbled 5.52% in a record single-session point loss amid an equity sell-off driven by artificial intelligence concerns and United States midterm anxieties. Technology shares led the decline, prompting duration buying in government bonds as a flight to safety compressed yields. Gold advanced toward its largest weekly gain since August in parallel with the risk-off rotation.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Wall Street rout spreads globally after record Nasdaq drop

stories.t: Nasdaq breaks point-loss record in sharp market sell-off
stories.src: Investor's Business Daily · BBC · Yahoo Finance
stories.b: The Nasdaq is an index, which is a list of shares tracked together to measure market health. It just suffered its biggest single-day point drop ever. Major tech companies saw their share prices plunge overnight. US midterms added to fears of an artificial intelligence slowdown. US Treasury yields dipped during the session.
stories.i: The Nasdaq composite suffered a record single-session point loss amid a broad market sell-off driven by artificial intelligence concerns and US midterm anxieties. Major technology shares plummeted, pushing the index down by 5.52%. Government bond yields drifted lower as investors sought safety in fixed income, while gold headed for its largest weekly gain since August.
stories.a: The Nasdaq composite shattered its single-session point-loss record during a steep tech-led correction catalysed by artificial intelligence growth fears and midterm political risks. US Treasury yields compressed as capital rotated away from risk assets into safe havens. Gold scaled towards its biggest weekly advance since August, reflecting broad duration demand amidst equity liquidations.

politics.b: US midterms added to fears of an artificial intelligence slowdown.
politics.i: US midterms compounded anxieties surrounding slowing artificial intelligence growth.
politics.a: US midterms intersected with structural concerns over artificial intelligence monetisation timelines.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: FTSE 100 dips following Bank of England rate hike to 4%

stories.t: Bank of England raises rates to 4%
stories.b: The Bank of England is the country's central bank, which sets official borrowing costs for the economy. It decided to push interest rates up to 4%. Higher rates make loans and mortgages more expensive for everyone. This change causes ripples across all financial markets. The official rate reached 4%.
stories.i: The Bank of England adjusted its monetary policy stance by lifting interest rates to 4%. This official rate increase raises the cost of capital throughout the financial system. Central banks tighten policy like this to cool domestic demand and inflation pressures. Commercial lenders quickly reprice their lending products to reflect the new benchmark. The benchmark rate sits at 4%.
stories.a: The Bank of England advanced its tightening cycle by raising the policy rate to 4%. This adjustment alters the short-term interest rate expectations embedded across sterling swap curves. Asset allocators responded by re-pricing risk assets as the hurdle rate for capital shifted upward. Terminal rate pricing adjusted higher following the decision. The benchmark rate reached 4%.

stories.t: FTSE 100 declines to 10,782.66
stories.b: The FTSE 100 is a major stock market index tracking the one hundred largest companies listed in London. Share prices across this index fell after the central bank announcement. The index closed down at a specific level. Investors reacted immediately to the tighter monetary conditions. The index finished the session at 10,782.66.
stories.i: The FTSE 100 equity index dropped in response to the tighter monetary policy stance. Large-cap equities faced selling pressure as higher borrowing costs dimmed corporate earnings outlooks. Market participants rebalanced portfolios away from risk-sensitive shares. The blue-chip index settled lower. The index ended trading at 10,782.66.
stories.a: The FTSE 100 equity benchmark reacted to the higher policy rate by contracting to 10,782.66. Equity risk premium requirements expanded as the risk-free rate shifted upward. Institutional investors adjusted duration and equity weightings to account for compressed corporate valuations. Broad selling concentrated in rate-sensitive sectors. The index closed at 10,782.66.

politics.b: Public debate centered on why borrowing costs are rising across the country. Officials at the central bank explained their rationale for adjusting rates. Citizens face higher expenses on loans and mortgages. The official rate reached 4%.
politics.i: Policymakers at the central bank defended the decision to tighten monetary policy. Officials pointed to underlying economic pressures driving the adjustment in interest rates. The policy rate move directly impacts household finances and corporate borrowing. The benchmark rate sits at 4%.
politics.a: Monetary authorities articulated the policy rationale for lifting the official rate to 4%. Policymakers balanced growth considerations against domestic price pressures. Transmission mechanisms remain a central focus for fiscal and monetary observers alike. The rate settled at 4%.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: DAX hits record high before closing lower

stories.t: DAX Reaches Record Peak Before Turning Negative
stories.b: An index is a basket of company shares that shows how a market is doing. Germany's main index, the DAX 40, climbed to an all-time high. Then it reversed direction as trading went on. The index closed down 0.43% at 26,325.01 points.
stories.i: Germany's DAX 40 index touched a record high during the session. Selling pressure later pushed the benchmark into negative territory. The index closed down 0.43% at 26,325.01.
stories.a: The DAX 40 breached a record high before succumbing to broad selling pressure. Intraday momentum reversed as regional technology and defence equities lagged. The benchmark settled down 0.43% at 26,325.01.

stories.t: Rheinmetall Outlook Downgrade Weighs on German Equities
stories.b: European shares fell as technology and defence sectors dropped. Rheinmetall shares tumbled after a forecast downgrade for the year 2026. Wall Street also saw a tumble in prices.
stories.i: European shares retreated as a technology selloff and defence sector weakness hit regional markets. Rheinmetall shares tumbled following a downward revision to its fiscal year 2026 outlook. Wall Street losses added to the downward pressure on Frankfurt trading.
stories.a: Rheinmetall shares fell sharply after management downgraded its fiscal year 2026 outlook. Sector-wide weakness in defence compounded a wider European technology selloff. US equity declines added cross-border headwinds that pressured Frankfurt equities.

politics.b: German market updates mention no government policy actions.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Japanese markets slide as technology shares tumble

stories.t: Nikkei Falls Sharply
stories.src: The Economic Times · The Japan Times
stories.b: Japan's main stock market index, called the Nikkei 225, dropped by more than 7%. A stock market index is a group of shares tracked together to show how a market is doing. This big drop happened because technology companies related to artificial intelligence fell on Wall Street in the United States. The Nikkei index fell below the key level of 60,000 points. The market rout pushed the index closer to a bear market, which is a term for when prices fall by 20% or more from recent highs.
stories.i: Japan's benchmark index, the Nikkei 225, tumbled more than 7% during the session. Technology valuations suffered following sharp AI-related declines on Wall Street. The selloff drove the Nikkei below the 60,000 threshold. The losses pushed the benchmark index near bear market territory as risk appetite deteriorated globally.
stories.a: The Nikkei 225 plummeted over 7%, breaching the 60,000 support level amidst a broader technology sector repricing. Contagion from Wall Street artificial intelligence equity declines accelerated domestic liquidations. The resultant compression in tech valuations propelled the index toward a bear market configuration.

stories.t: State Asset Sales and Currency Shifts
stories.b: Prime Minister Takaichi announced that profits from selling Bank of Japan exchange-traded funds will fund a new economic security special account. Exchange-traded funds are baskets of investments that trade on public exchanges like stocks. Meanwhile, the Japanese yen pulled back from its weekly high against the United States dollar. The dollar held steady as traders awaited the United States non-farm payrolls employment report.
stories.i: Prime Minister Takaichi stated that gains from Bank of Japan exchange-traded fund sales will finance a new economic security special account. Elsewhere, the Japanese yen retreated from a weekly high. The United States dollar held firm as currency markets positioned ahead of the upcoming non-farm payrolls report.
stories.a: Prime Minister Takaichi earmarked Bank of Japan exchange-traded fund liquidation gains for a newly established economic security special account. Concurrently, the Japanese yen retraced from weekly highs against the greenback. The United States dollar consolidated gains as macro participants awaited United States non-farm payrolls data.

politics.b: Prime Minister Takaichi spoke about funding a special account using proceeds from central bank asset sales.
politics.i: Prime Minister Takaichi outlined plans to direct Bank of Japan asset sale proceeds toward an economic security special account.
politics.a: Prime Minister Takaichi detailed the fiscal allocation of Bank of Japan exchange-traded fund realization gains toward an economic security special account.

timeline: Nikkei 225 drops over 7% below 60,000 points following Wall Street technology losses.

stories.t: Hainan Duty-Free Revenue
stories.b: Hainan started a new tax-free shopping policy for visitors. This policy logged $5bn in sales during its first year. Duty-free means buyers do not pay certain local import taxes.
stories.i: Hainan implemented a fresh offshore duty-free policy. Total sales reached $5bn in the first year of operation under these rules.
stories.a: Hainan recorded $5bn in transactions during the initial twelve months of its offshore duty-free framework. The turnover metrics quantify the policy's early retail capture in the region.

stories.t: Yuan Valuation Pressures
stories.b: The Chinese yuan faces a tricky dilemma. It is too weak abroad but looks too strong at home. Central bank resistance caps how much the currency is allowed to appreciate.
stories.i: The Chinese yuan navigates a split valuation framework. Authorities moderate the pace of currency appreciation while managing external pressures.
stories.a: The People's Bank of China maintains resistance that caps currency appreciation. Analysts at Societe Generale and OCBC track authorities moderating the speed of gains while divergence persists.

India.label: India
India.sub: Indian indices post large gains and overseas funds pump in capital

stories.t: Sensex and Nifty record largest single-day gains in seven months
stories.b: The Sensex and the Nifty are stock market indexes, which are big baskets of shares used to track how the overall stock market is doing. They just had their biggest single-day gains in seven months. The Sensex went up by 6,064 points over six days. This puts the market on track for its strongest pre-Diwali rally in 35 years.
stories.i: The Sensex and the Nifty recorded their biggest single-day gains in seven months. The Sensex climbed 6,064 points over six days. This momentum puts the benchmark on track for its strongest pre-Diwali rally in 35 years.
stories.a: Indian equity benchmarks logged their largest single-day percentage gains in seven months following an aggressive six-session expansion totalling 6,064 points on the Sensex. The velocity of the advance puts the index on course for its most robust pre-Diwali performance in 35 years, despite the Nifty facing an expected opening pullback of approximately 170 points.

stories.t: Overseas investors pour capital into domestic shares as rupee edges up
stories.src: The Economic Times · The Times of India
stories.b: Overseas funds pumped Rs 14,975 crore into the Sensex rally. At the same time, the Indian rupee gained 16 paise against other currencies. Analysts are also looking at different investment products like real estate investment trusts, which have beaten the Nifty over the past two years.
stories.i: Overseas funds pumped Rs 14,975 crore into domestic equities during the rally. Simultaneously, the rupee advanced by 16 paise. Separately, listed real estate investment trusts outperformed the Nifty over a two-year horizon.
stories.a: Institutional flows surged as overseas funds injected Rs 14,975 crore into Indian equities, coinciding with a 16-paise appreciation in the rupee. Meanwhile, comparative yield evaluations show listed real estate investment trusts outperforming the Nifty over a two-year timeframe.

politics.b: There are no political updates in the market reports today.
politics.i: No government or policy announcements were covered in the financial reports.
politics.a: No direct political developments or policy shifts were reported in the session updates.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras projects and interest rate decisions

stories.t: Petrobras Expands Operations and Prepares for Earnings
stories.src: Marketscreener · Brazil Energy Insight · Yahoo Finance
stories.b: Petrobras is the giant state-run oil company of Brazil. It manages massive oil fields beneath the ocean floor. The company is currently drilling a second well in the Norte de Brava block located in the Campos Basin. At the same time, Petrobras has increased its diesel imports for November to rebuild its fuel stocks following maintenance work at its refineries.
stories.i: Petrobras advances its offshore development by drilling a second well in the Norte de Brava block within the Campos Basin pre-salt region. Management simultaneously scales up November diesel imports to replenish inventories after completing scheduled refinery maintenance. These operational updates precede the upcoming release of third-quarter financial results.
stories.a: Petrobras drives offshore production momentum with the spudding of a secondary well in the Norte de Brava pre-salt structure. Inventory management reflects proactive supply adjustments via elevated November diesel imports following domestic refining outages. Markets await third-quarter earnings disclosures to gauge cash flow conversion amid record output metrics.

stories.t: Brazil Holds Benchmark Interest Rate at 13.75%
stories.b: Central banks use interest rates to control the cost of borrowing money across the country. Brazil kept its benchmark interest rate, known as the Selic rate, steady at 13.75%. This decision keeps Brazil at the top of global rankings for real interest rates when adjusted for local price changes. Industrial groups have raised concerns about how these high borrowing costs impact the broader economy.
stories.i: The Central Bank of Brazil maintains the Selic rate at 13.75%, securing the country's position at the apex of the global real interest rate rankings. Policymakers opted to hold borrowing costs steady despite mounting pressure from the industrial sector regarding economic growth constraints. The ongoing monetary stance reflects efforts to anchor domestic price stability.
stories.a: Monetary authorities preserve the Selic rate at 13.75%, cementing Brazil's status at the top of sovereign real interest rate league tables. Industrial constituents continue to challenge the prevailing macroeconomic framework amid stringent monetary conditions. Transmission channels remain constricted as lending costs suppress cyclical demand vectors.

politics.b: Industrial leaders in Brazil are openly challenging the country's economic strategy. They argue that high interest rates hurt domestic manufacturing companies. The government continues to defend its monetary approach while managing state-owned energy operations.
politics.i: Brazilian industrial sectors voice mounting friction against the established economic framework. Manufacturing lobbyists argue that elevated borrowing costs stifle domestic expansion. Policy consistency remains anchored to fiscal and monetary discipline despite political pushback.
politics.a: Industrial stakeholders contest the prevailing economic tripod framework amid restrictive monetary settings. Policy architecture withstands sectoral lobbying pressure while state enterprise Petrobras executes offshore extraction targets. Institutional commitment to orthodox policy levers persists without structural deviation.

timeline: Brazil holds the Selic rate steady at 13.75%

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira depreciation, fiscal deficits, and banking fraud probes

stories.t: Naira Depreciation and Interbank Turnover
stories.b: The naira is the official money used in Nigeria. Its value fell against the United States dollar recently. Trading activity in the foreign exchange market dropped by 19% at the same time. Fewer dollars were moving through the interbank system.
stories.i: The naira extended its depreciation against the USD as interbank foreign exchange turnover moderated by 19%. This lower transaction volume reflects constrained liquidity in the official currency market. Lower turnover often compounds downward pressure on the exchange rate.
stories.a: Interbank FX turnover contracted by 19%, coinciding with the ongoing depreciation of the naira against the dollar. This liquidity contraction in the domestic market exacerbates spot rate volatility and widens spreads against parallel market rates like the ₦1,377 per dollar handle. Reduced transaction flows limit price discovery efficiency for commercial participants.

stories.t: Fiscal Deficits and Borrowing Impact
stories.b: The Central Bank of Nigeria released a report about government money shortfalls. When a government spends more money than it collects, it runs a deficit. This shortfall hurts the local currency and pushes up interest rates. Officials are also looking at taking on a new foreign loan of $7.7bn.
stories.i: A Central Bank of Nigeria report showed that persistent fiscal deficits continue to hurt the naira and spike interest rates. Government borrowing needs drive up local borrowing costs across the economy. Discussions around a $7.7bn external debt addition compound these fiscal pressures.
stories.a: Central Bank of Nigeria disclosures indicate that sovereign fiscal deficits are the primary transmission channel driving naira weakness and higher local interest rate yields. Public sector borrowing requirements crowd out private credit demand while elevating default risks. Parliamentary and executive debates over securing an additional $7.7bn in external financing highlight structural budget imbalances.

stories.t: EFCC Investigates Former Bank Manager
stories.b: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission is investigating an ex-bank manager. The official is accused of taking money that belonged to a customer. The missing amount is N515m.
stories.i: Anti-corruption authorities opened a formal investigation into a former bank manager. The suspect allegedly diverted N515m from a client account. The EFCC continues to question the individual regarding the missing funds.
stories.a: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission initiated a probe into an ex-bank manager over the alleged diversion of N515m from a customer account. Financial crimes investigations of this nature expose institutional internal control vulnerabilities within commercial depositories. Regulatory compliance checks are expected to face stricter enforcement following the incident.

politics.b: Lawmakers and former officials discussed problems in the government budget. A former Air Force spokesperson pointed out a flaw in the multi-trillion naira defense budget. Meanwhile, the government announced a N50,000 free support program for users of the OPay platform.
politics.i: Defense budget allocations faced scrutiny after a former Air Force spokesperson identified structural flaws in national security spending. Government officials also advanced social intervention plans, detailing disbursement mechanisms for N50,000 cash grants to OPay users.
politics.a: National security expenditure frameworks drew sharp criticism as a former Air Force spokesperson detailed structural implementation flaws in multi-trillion naira defense appropriations. Concurrently, executive agencies progressed populist fiscal distributions, outlining modalities for distributing N50,000 monetary grants via the OPay platform to targeted citizens.

Australia.sub: ASX indices move on sector updates and banking support

stories.t: Banks Support ASX as Consumer Staples and Travel Shares Advance
stories.b: The Australian stock market survives a drop on Wall Street because local banks step in to help. Consumer staples companies see their share prices rise. Mining companies experience a slide in their share values. Travel demand stays strong in fiscal year 2027, which pushes the share price of Qantas higher.
stories.i: The Australian securities exchange withstands negative pressure from Wall Street, supported by gains in the banking sector. Consumer staples outperform while miners face downward revisions. Meanwhile, persistent travel demand through fiscal year 2027 underpins equity appreciation for Qantas.
stories.a: Domestic financials insulate the local benchmark from overnight offshore volatility while sector dispersion splits consumer staples and mining operators. Persistent structural demand for travel into fiscal year 2027 continues to re-rate transport equities higher, assuming current margin assumptions hold against input cost pressures.

stories.t: Corporate Earnings and Growth Updates Across Australian Equities
stories.b: DroneShield reports record half-year revenue alongside a statutory loss. Data#3 positions itself for artificial intelligence and security demand following its fiscal year 2026 result. Codan guides to a more encouraging first half after completing a record fiscal year 2026. CAR Group balances its mature Australian operations with international growth initiatives.
stories.i: DroneShield reconciles record half-year revenue with a statutory loss in its financial filings. Data#3 details its strategic positioning for artificial intelligence and cybersecurity demand post-FY26. Codan issues positive guidance for the upcoming half following record FY26 metrics, while CAR Group manages domestic maturity alongside overseas expansion.
stories.a: Operational divergence emerges as DroneShield pairs top-line record revenue with statutory net losses, while Data#3 pivots capital expenditure toward artificial intelligence and security verticals post-FY26. Codan guides toward a stronger front-half trajectory off record historical earnings bases. CAR Group balances cash-generative domestic maturity against offshore growth vectors.
